source:
let's make a car game that focuses on Holden vs Ford, but obviously with copyright free names.
we use "iron lion" as the Holden variant, and "blue wolf" as the ford variant, with trims being similar in letters, but the difference? the VE ute is a VA ute.
engines: Iron lion 5.0L V8 petrol (200kw, 300nm of torque) yes we will have power and torque specs here.. but in metric only with imperial measurements available in settings.
like a toggle.
obviously the standard reading is in kmh tho you can opt for mph or both at once, and the only drive side is right hand drive, this game takes the appearance of a new Zealand south island City (specifically eastern Christchurch around Buckley's road) turned into a sort of Roblox variant, where some locations are moved around so it doesn't replicate the real city too much, and the cars you get to actually see your character shifting gears, you can flick the indicator stalks even on mobile, and you can get a completely ai made instrumental version of copyrighted music to actually avoid copyright while having a jam.
for example, the song "jaded" by new Zealand based band racing, is a copyright protected song, so we use an instrumental different name for the song, calling it emeralded divinity.. but as an instrumental of that song.
tame impala - Dracula is then called tamed feline - vampire (instrumental, full)
each soundtrack spanning over 3 to 5 minutes.
anyways, on the car's interior, you get proper controls, and you even get a manual transmission interface when you hop into a manual iron lion vs an automatic iron lion which gives you a manual mode.
also, in the manuals, you get a clutch pedal.
which you can see your character use.
in the tutorial, it shows the pattern: clutch in, shift, apply throttle optionally, clutch out, repeat if needed.
you can even choose engines to swap into cars the more money you get via racing NPCs, racing players, or even just by playing the game or by playing a simulation using the car, or a "stop the lever In the green zone" minigame that always rewards you even if you lose it.
engines in this game include: diesel (inline 4, inline six, inline 5, V6, V8, V6 TT, V12 5.0L NA petrol, and many more petrols, like I3 to I9 and V2 to V28 (28L V28) located in a giant motorhome.
the starter car you get is based on a Toyota crown royal saloon 2.5L V6, it's the Toyokao Crow loyal salmon 2.5P 6AT.. or a manual altezza? it's the raltezzo SR200S beans, 87 octane to 100 octane petrols available mostly just 91 to 98 tho, and an Australian ford falcon XR6 twin turbo based copyright free ute appears.

answers.ask: Is this free-roam driving with optional street races, or are the races the main loop with a proper track?
answers.answer: This is free-roam driving in a Roblox-inspired eastern Christchurch, with optional races against NPCs and players as the main ways to earn money alongside normal play and simulation/minigames. Do not make a separate proper track the core loop.

answers.ask: How much of eastern Christchurch should the map cover, and which landmarks must be recognisable?
answers.answer: Keep it to a small, condensed area inspired by eastern Christchurch around Buckleys Road, with roads and locations moved around so it is not a replica. No real landmarks need to be recognisable; use a generic New Zealand South Island suburban-city look.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D free-roam driving map set in a small, condensed Roblox-inspired New Zealand South Island suburban city, loosely inspired by eastern Christchurch around Buckleys Road without replicating real locations. Build a right-hand-traffic street network of broad suburban roads, intersections, side streets, parking areas, low-rise commercial buildings, homes, and generic city-edge spaces, with locations rearranged into an original layout. Include open roadside and parking areas suitable for optional NPC and player street-race meetups, plus a giant motorhome displayed as a notable vehicle/engine-related prop. The drivable vehicle roster includes copyright-free Iron Lion and Blue Wolf performance variants, utility vehicles, and starter sedan/coupe options, with visible detailed interiors for driver seating, dashboard controls, gear shifters, indicator stalks, pedals, and manual-transmission layouts.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Simulation, specifically free-roam vehicle simulation; optional street races do not make this a track-based Racing map. No secondary genre is needed because there is no designated race route.

### Shape and preset
Use `world-shared`, a single connected suburban driving district rather than isolated player plots or a circuit. Match the Vehicle Sim preset for its shared drivable world and roadway emphasis, but omit its shared extraction-field option because the prompt describes a city, not resource hauling.

### Config requirements
`path-road-vehicle` is visible geometry: a right-hand-traffic network of broad, vehicle-turnable suburban roads, intersections, side streets, and parking circulation. `settlement-density` is visible geometry: a compact low-rise suburban-city fabric of houses and commercial buildings. No building-enterable option is selected; the requested detailed interiors belong to the displayed vehicles, not to city buildings.

### Layout components
Build one condensed, original city district loosely evoking eastern Christchurch around Buckleys Road without reproducing real streets or landmarks. Place a main broad arterial running diagonally across the plan, with several signalized or clearly marked intersections feeding a loose grid of side streets. Put low-rise commercial strips, forecourts, and broad parking areas along the arterial; place quieter residential blocks and detached homes beyond them. Include generic city-edge ground at the outskirts—open verges, sparse lots, and low development—to keep the district from reading as a dense downtown.

Use open roadside pull-offs and two or more generous parking areas as informal optional race-meetup spaces, connected directly to the normal street network rather than isolated as a proper circuit. Feature one giant motorhome prominently in a commercial or parking-side display area as the engine-related landmark. Populate parking and roadside display areas with copyright-free Iron Lion and Blue Wolf performance cars, utility vehicles, and starter sedan/coupe vehicles. Show selected vehicles with visible driver seating, dashboards, gear shifters, indicator stalks, pedals, and manual-layout details. Bound the map with original suburban edge roads, planted verges, fencing, and distant low cityscape rather than recognizable real-world landmarks. Frame the main arterial and motorhome as the strongest isometric read.

### Render order
Use `topdown`: the connected, right-hand-traffic road hierarchy and intersection access need to remain legible and driveable before the isometric view dresses the suburb.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is medium, driven by a compact but complete road district with commercial, residential, parking, and city-edge zones. Theme: Roblox-inspired New Zealand South Island suburb, broad practical roads, modest low-rise buildings, and performance-car culture. Use `P0`; this is one exterior ground surface with no forced overhangs, interiors, separate maps, or volumetric play.
